title: Sodachapped hands
html_source:
In Calypso it is clear what Leopold is thinking though not why as opposed to Stephen’s disjointed thoughts in Proteus. Having been privvy to Leopold’s enjoyment of seeing the woman, we now hear his negative thoughts about the reality of his brief fantasy.

Chapped hands and crusted toenails introduce the reader to Bloom’s tendency to weigh things up but don’t go near prepping us for the horrific chain of thoughts which culminate in the shocking regard he has for the female state in four paragraphs time:
‘Dead: an old woman’s: the grey sunken cunt of the
world.’
The contrast between the ordinary, the clear thoughts about Jewish settlements and the negative internal monologue sequence adds to the suspense of the chapter. The reader knows nothing yet of Bloom’s knowledge of Molly’s affair with Boylan, very possibly what has lead to the internal negative narrative.
